items.name: the Horse
items.description: The huge wooden horse built by Epeius, in which the Greek chiefs hide to enter and sack Troy.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Trojan Horse was a wooden horse said to have been used by the Greeks during the Trojan War to sneak into the city of Troy and win the war. The Trojan Horse is not mentioned in Homer's Iliad, with the poem ending before the war is concluded, and it is only briefly mentioned in the Odyssey.

items.name: the arms of Achilles
items.description: Achilles' divine armour and shield; Thetis offers it as a prize, Odysseus wins it, and Neoptolemus later wears it.

items.name: the shield of Achilles
items.description: Achilles' great shield, its scenes described in detail when Thetis lays out his arms.

wikipedia.lead: The shield of Achilles is the shield that Achilles uses in his fight with Hector, as described in a passage in Book 18, lines 478–608 of Homer's Iliad. The intricately detailed imagery on the shield has inspired many different interpretations of its significance.

items.name: the arms of Hercules
items.description: The bow and arrows of Hercules, used by Philoctetes to wound Paris.

items.name: the sword of Hector
items.description: The sword with which Aias kills himself after his madness.

items.name: the arms of Memnon
items.description: Armour taken from Memnon, won by Aias with the iron bar at Achilles' games.

items.name: the shield of Hercules
items.description: Shield carried by Eurypylus, decorated with the labours of Hercules.

items.name: the aegis
items.description: Zeus' awful shield-like cloak, whose weapons he gives to Athena for vengeance.

wikipedia.lead: The aegis or egis, as stated in the Iliad, is a device carried by Zeus, Apollo and Athena, variously interpreted as an animal skin or a shield and sometimes featuring the head of a Gorgon. There may be a connection with a deity named Aex, a daughter of Helios and a nurse of Zeus or alternatively a mistress of Zeus (Hyginus, Astronomica 2.
